case_name: State of Maharashtra v Rajendra and others
facts: The appeals are directed against the judgment dated 18th August, 2005 passed by the High Court of Judicature at Bombay, Nagpur Bench, Nagpur.
Marriage of deceased took place with accused No.2-Rajendra on 19th April, 1998.
The deceased sustained 98% burn injuries in the early morning of 8th April, 1999, in her matrimonial house i.e. the house of the accused Nos.1, 2, 3, 5 and 6.

Prosecution case is that the husband and the mother-in-law i.e. accused Nos.2 and 3 used to beat the deceased whereas other accused together with accused Nos.2 and 3 used to mentally and physically ill-treat the deceased on account of dowry demand.
The parents of the deceased immediately rushed to Mayo Hospital. It was found that their daughter was already dead.
A.D. No.28/99 u/s. 174 Cr.P.C. was registered at 10.50 a.m. on 8th April, 1999 on the basis of report of Police Head Constable Diwakar from Mayo Hospital Police Booth.

The further investigation was carried out by Police Sub-Inspector, Parvekar. He recorded the statement of the father of deceased and arrested accused No.2-Rajendra i.e. husband of the deceased on 8th April, 1999 itself.

Viscera of the deceased that was preserved at the time of the postmortem examination, pieces of saree, match box and a piece of burnt plastic which were seized at the time of drawing the panchanama were forwarded to the Chemical Analyser for examination.
The marriage ceremony of the deceased and accused No.2-Rajendra was shot by a video shooting. Its video cassette was produced by the complainant before the Investigating Officer.
Charges for offence punishable under Sections 498-A, 304-B, 306 r/w 34 IPC were framed to which the accused pleaded not guilty.
The prosecution produced altogether 14 witnesses.
The defence, as how it appears from the cross-examination of the witnesses etc. is that of total denial with regard to the alleged cruelty.
The stand was that the accused always gave good treatment to the deceased. They gave jewellery to the deceased and also invested money in her name in the post office.
It was denied that they ever demanded any dowry from her parents.
Deceased's family informed that they are unable to pay more than what was already agreed.
The accused No1 did not take any meals or food during the marriage.
A golden chain of about 12 gms. was presented to accused No.2.
Accused No.2 was refusing to accept the said chain and wanted the chain of 2 tolas (20 gms.) and the golden stick.
The deceased had to come back to her parents house after 8-10 days of the marriage.
She disclosed that her in-laws were torturing her throughout the day for not giving the T.V. set, Cooler, Almirah and Hero Honda Motorcycle.
After 3-4 months of the marriage they had given an amount of Rs.20,000/- to accused No.2 for Almirah, Cooler and T.V., still the torture was continued.
The deceased-Ranjana used to come to her parents' house whenever called by them.
Accused No.2-Rajendra used to take the deceased to the house of her parents at an interval of 3-4 days on some pretext or other.
She further stated that Ranjana had stayed with her for a span of 3-4 days when she had come after 8-10 days of marriage.
Thereafter she was not sent for residing, however, she was sent in January for 2-3 days.
petitioner_arguments: The prosecution has proved the demand of dowry and cruelty for the said demand.
All ingredients for conviction under Sections 498-A and 304-B IPC were present.
It was presumed that the case was that of a dowry death.
The deceased had to come back to her parents house after 8-10 days of the marriage.
She disclosed that her in-laws were torturing her throughout the day for not giving the T.V. set, Cooler, Almirah and Hero Honda Motorcycle.
After 3-4 months of the marriage they had given an amount of Rs.20,000/- to accused No.2 for Almirah, Cooler and T.V., still the torture was continued.
respondent_arguments: The deposition of prosecution witnesses after five years was improved version from their version made during the investigation.
They added allegation to attract Section 304B IPC.
All were related to the deceased.
Thus they were interested witnesses and their credibility is considerably in question.
It was denied that they ever demanded any dowry from her parents.
The accused always gave good treatment to the deceased. They gave jewellery to the deceased and also invested money in her name in the post office.
The stand was that of total denial with regard to the alleged cruelty.
court_reasoning: The High Court recorded completely erroneous finding that prosecution has not proved suicidal death of Ranjana.
In fact, the defence itself came with the story of suicidal death of Ranjana.
The impugned judgment is cryptic, unreasoned and order of acquittal was passed without discussion and appreciation of evidence.
The stand of the respondents is that the deposition of prosecution witnesses after five years was improved version from their version made during the investigation.
All were related to the deceased. Thus they were interested witnesses and their credibility is considerably in question.
holding: The impugned judgment dated 18th August, 2005 passed by the High Court of Judicature at Bombay, Nagpur Bench, Nagpur was set aside.
The appeals are allowed and the accused-respondents are acquitted from the charges under Section 498-A, Section 304-B and S.306 IPC all read with S.34 IPC.
